sugars can enhance the performance of enzymes in organic media, but their mechanism of action is still not completely understood and further studies are required to elucidate their role.
sugars, both monosaccharides and disaccharide, have a positive effect on the activity and the enantioselectiviy of lipase B. from Burkholderia Cepacia in organic solvents.

sugars, in addition to their well-known role in protecting proteins from dehydration, can be used to improve the catalytic properties of enzymes in organic solvents by reducing the deleterious interactions among the enzyme molecules and by preventing the formation of protein aggregates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of sugars can significantly enhance the activity and the enantioselective properties of lipase from Burkolderia cepacia in organic solvent.
the use of mono- or disaccharides is an easy and cheap way to improve the activity and enantiomeric excess of lipases in organic solvents without significantly altering their conformation.
sugars are not just inert molecules that stabilize proteins in organic solvent, but that they are able to modulate protein structure and activity.
